subject.title: Add atomic claim/lease primitives for concurrent cron job dispatch and removal

question: Which public cron concurrency contract should OpenClaw support for dispatch/remove races: full lease tokens, compare-and-set removal, or an internal single-flight guarantee with documentation?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but the durable API shape, conflict exit code, caller retry behavior, and whether a lease token should become part of wake payloads require maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Add narrow CAS/remove preconditions
options.body: Add an `--if-unclaimed` or expected-version remove path with a documented conflict result before considering a broader lease-token payload contract.

options.title: Design full lease tokens
options.body: Expose dispatch claims with token, holder, expiry, revocation behavior, and wake-payload validation for callers that need strict in-flight authority.

options.title: Document internal single-flight only
options.body: Keep the public remove surface small and instead enforce and document non-overlap/dropped-wake semantics if maintainers do not want a caller-visible claim API.

recommendation.title: Add narrow CAS/remove preconditions
recommendation.body: Add an `--if-unclaimed` or expected-version remove path with a documented conflict result before considering a broader lease-token payload contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current-main cron remove, timer, and Gateway schema history points to steipete as the best available owner for the API direction choice.
